previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of common variable immunodeficiency, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and Hodgkin’s lymphoma status post allogeneic stem cell transplant presented with acute abdominal pain and markedly increased watery ostomy output. She was febrile on admission with CT findings of small bowel wall thickening suggestive of enteritis. Infectious workup was negative for C. difficile, bacterial pathogens, parasites, and CMV, with stool viral culture also negative. Symptoms improved with supportive care, including IV fluids and electrolyte repletion. She was discharged home after clinical improvement on a short course of oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, with instructions to complete potassium supplementation and follow up with her transplant and oncology teams.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PA AND LAT)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with history of stem cell transplant, now with
fever  // evaluate for cause of fever      evaluate for cause of fever

COMPARISON:  Comparison to prior study dated ___ at 15:55

FINDINGS: 

PA and lateral views of the chest ___ at 15:30 are submitted

IMPRESSION: 

Right subclavian Port-A-Cath unchanged in position.  Lungs appear well
inflated without evidence of focal airspace consolidation to suggest
pneumonia.  No pleural effusions, pulmonary edema or pneumothorax.  Stable
cardiac and mediastinal contours.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with new RLQ pain in setting of CMV viremia,
s/p MUD allo, GI GVHD // r/o infectious etiology such as typhlitis vs
appendicitis?

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
IV Contrast: 130 mL Omnipaque.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:   Total DLP (Body) = 239 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis performed ___.

FINDINGS: 

Chest:  New relative to prior examination is left lower lobe ___
opacities. There is no pleural effusion. There is no pericardial effusion.

Abdomen:  The liver appears homogeneous in attenuation without a focal lesion
identified. There is no intrahepatic biliary duct dilation. The portal veins
are patent. No focal lesions identified within the liver.  The gallbladder is
without radiopaque cholelithiasis and otherwise unremarkable. Prominence of
the common bile duct with smooth tapering distally to the ampulla of is not
significantly changed relative to prior examination. The pancreas is without
pancreatic duct dilation.  Splenomegaly is mild and unchanged. No focal
splenic lesion is identified.  Bilateral adrenal glands are normal in
appearance.

The kidneys present symmetric nephrograms and excretion of contrast.  There is
no hydronephrosis or perinephric fluid collection.

The stomach and duodenum are unremarkable.  Patient is status post small bowel
resection as indicated by suture material within the lower mid abdomen
(05:56).  Patient is status post sigmoid colon and descending colon resection
with left lower quadrant end-colostomy.  Relative to prior examination dated ___, there has been interval near resolution of diffuse small bowel
wall thickening, edema, and mucosal hyper enhancement.  Trace amount of
nonhemorrhagic fluid within the right lower quadrant interloops is associated
with mild wall thickening and edema of the distal ileum (7:25). The appendix
is visualized, normal in caliber and without surrounding inflammatory changes.
The ascending and transverse colon to the level of the colostomy is
unremarkable.

Trace abdominal free fluid layers within the right lower quadrant (5:66). 
There is no abdominal free air.  The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber
without aneurysmal dilatation. Scattered retroperitoneal nodes appear to have
been present on prior examination. To the left of the aorta at the level of
the kidneys is a 1.1 x 0.8 cm node previously 1.1 x 0.8 cm (05:35).  A
periaortic node currently measures 0.9 x 0.7 cm (05:33), previously 0.8 x 0.6
cm, not significantly changed.  An there is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric
adenopathy which meet CT size criteria for pathology.

Pelvis: The bladder is moderately well distended, grossly unremarkable.  There
is no pelvic free fluid.  There is no inguinal or pelvic sidewall adenopathy.

Posterior spinal hardware traverses the L5-S1 vertebral bodies, unchanged. 
There is no bony lesion worrisome for malignancy or infection. Postsurgical
changes involve the right iliac bone consistent with bone graft donor site.

IMPRESSION: 

1. New left lower lobe tree-in ___ opacities is worrisome for either focal
aspiration or alternatively bronchocentric infectious process.
2. Normal appendi and cecum. No evidence of typhlitis.
3. Near resolution of previously identified diffuse small bowel wall
thickening, edema and mucosal hyperenhancement with small amount of distal
ileal wall edema associated with a tiny amount of interloop free fluid.
4. Status post small bowel resection, sigmoid resection and descending colon
resection with left lower quadrant end colostomy. No evidence of obstruction.

EXAMINATION:  CT CHEST W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with new tree in ___ opacities // evaluate LLL
for new tree in ___ opacities noted on CT Abd

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector helical scanning of the chest was performed without
intravenous contrast agent reconstructed as contiguous 5- and 1.25-mm thick
axial, 2.5-mm thick coronal and parasagittal, and 8 x 8 mm MIPs axial images.

DOSE:   Acquisition sequence: 1) CT Localizer Radiograph 2) CT Localizer
Radiograph 3) Spiral Acquisition 6.1 s, 43.9 cm; CTDIvol = 5.7 mGy (Body) DLP
= 225.0 mGy-cm. Total DLP (Body) = 225 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis dated ___, CT chest dated ___, and ___.

FINDINGS: 

The thyroid is normal.  A right-sided Port-A-Cath terminates the lower SVC. 
There are no pathologically enlarged supraclavicular, axillary, mediastinal or
hilar lymph nodes.

The aorta and pulmonary arteries are normal in size.  The heart is normal in
size and demonstrates mild coronary artery calcifications. There is no
pericardial effusion.

No pneumothorax or pleural effusion is identified. The airways are patent to
the subsegmental level.  Lung windows demonstrate a stable, 1.2 cm
perifissural pulmonary nodule in the left lower lobe which is unchanged from
at least ___. There is diffuse bronchial wall thickening.

Regions of ground-glass and ___ opacities are seen within the inferior
left upper lobe and left lower lobe, all of which appear new from the prior
examination dated ___.  Similar opacities are noted within the
right lower lobe, albeit much less severe as compared to the left side. 
Multiple bilateral millimetric pulmonary nodules and calcified granulomas are
also stable.  Scarring is noted at the bilateral lung apices.

No suspicious osseous lesions are identified.

Mild ascites is noted within the upper abdomen.  For full description of the
intra-abdominal contents, please see the separate CT abdomen and pelvis
examination performed on ___.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Interval development of extensive ___ and ground-glass opacities
within the bilateral lower lobes and inferior portion of the left upper lobe,
worrisome for endobronchial spread of active infection, probably due to virus
or mycoplasma.
2.  No new, suspicious pulmonary nodules or masses.
3. For full description of the intra-abdominal contents, please see the
separate CT abdomen and pelvis examination performed on ___.

EXAMINATION:  UNILAT LOWER EXT VEINS LEFT

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with DLBCL // now with unilateral leg swelling
(L>R), r/o DVT

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed
on the left lower extremity veins.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

There is normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation of the left common
femoral, femoral, and popliteal veins.  Evaluation of the calf veins is
somewhat limited with normal color flow demonstrated in the posterior tibial
veins but evaluation of the peroneal veins was limited.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.

No evidence of medial popliteal fossa (___) cyst.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of deep venous thrombosis in the visualized left lower
extremity veins.  Limited evaluation of the peroneal veins.
